messages.subject: time series interpulation
parts:
Hi 

I have a time series on approximately a weekly basis
g1=
       date1       site   nitrate
1   2018-01-17 1    270.39 
2   2018-01-23 1    108.30 
3   2018-01-31 1     42.08 
4   2018-02-06 1     65.47 
5   2018-02-07 1     45.16 
6   2018-02-21 1     70.01 
7   2018-02-27 1     60.07 
8   2018-03-13 1    109.57 
9   2018-03-14 1     22.55 
10  2018-03-15 1     47.24
24 2018-02-07 2     23.94 
25  2018-02-21 2     53.23 
26  2018-02-27 2     32.15 
27  2018-03-13 2     31.97 
28  2018-03-13 2     31.86 
29  2018-03-15 2     34.93 
30  2018-03-23 2     32.60 
31  2018-04-05 2     35.99 

there are 8 sites...

I would like to get an interpolation for a daily nitrate, for each site.
is there a way to consider the site?
the following works, but i need to filter each site separately

g11<-filter(g1,site==1)
g2<-g11[,c("date1","nitrate")]

x <- zoo(g2$nitrate,g2$date1) 

x.new <- zoo(NA, seq(min(time(x)), to =  max(time(x)),by="day")) 

x.new[time(x)] <- x 

na.approx(x.new) 

Thanks,

Hanna

I recently discovered the wonderful map function in the purrr package. I would make a nested data frame by site and proceed like attached. I didn't get all the way through but you can probably follow along to see how to finish it up. This code could be condensed a lot but I wrote it out separately to make it easier to follow.
You can also save the nested results to a file for each element fairly easily with map2. Happy to help with this if needed.

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: time series interpulation
parts:
Hi

I would second Katherine: write a clean function that does the operation for one site, and which returns a data frame (instead of zoo). Then use the nest() and map() and unnest() function:

## pseudo data:
library(zoo)
library(tidyverse)

df <- expand.grid(date1 = as.Date(c(1, 2, 5, 6)),
            site = c(1, 2)) %>%
  mutate(nitrate = rnorm(8)) %>%
  as_data_frame

## your function:
my_function <- function(x) {
 
  x <- zoo(x$nitrate, x$date1)

x.new <- zoo(NA, seq(min(time(x)), to =  max(time(x)),by="day"))
  x.new[time(x)] <- x

res <- na.approx(x.new)
  data_frame(date = index(res),
             nitrate = as.numeric(res))
 
}

## test on 1
my_function(x=filter(df, site==1))


## apply to all
df %>%
  nest(-site) %>%
  mutate(new = map(data, my_function)) %>%
  unnest(new)
